author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Nigeria's Dangote Refinery, built on reclaimed wetlands in Lekki after about a decade of construction, has become one of Africa's largest industrial projects and is now at the centre of the continent's largest-ever share sale. The $20bn facility covers 2,635 hectares and can process 650,000 barrels of crude oil a day, more than Nigeria's four state-owned refineries combined. The refinery has been operating since 2024 and has helped reduce Nigeria's reliance on imported fuel, while providing greater protection against supply disruptions linked to the US-Israel war on Iran. The Dangote Group is now seeking about $1.6bn through a public share offering as it looks to raise up to $5bn from public and private investors. Aliko Dangote says the refinery's importance is not only about fuel prices but ensuring availability for Nigeria's large population during global supply disruptions. The company also plans to double the refinery's output and expand its reach across regional markets.

title: Dangote Refinery at centre of Africa's largest-ever share sale

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The Strait of Hormuz is a critical global energy chokepoint through which about 20 percent of the world's oil supply passes each day. The narrow passage between Iran and Oman operates through designated shipping lanes, but the US-Israel war on Iran has increased uncertainty and risks for vessels navigating the strait. Several countries have alternative routes, including Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the UAE's pipeline to Fujairah and Iraq's Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline, while some shipping can be diverted around the Cape of Good Hope. But these alternatives cannot match Hormuz's capacity of about 20 million barrels of oil a day, making prolonged disruption a major threat to global energy supplies. Iran also has land and rail routes through Pakistan, Türkiye and the Caspian region, but these are slower, more expensive and far smaller than maritime trade. 

Al Jazeera's Osama Bin Javaid explains how the Strait of Hormuz functions and why it remains difficult to replace.

title: How the Strait of Hormuz works and why it matters to global oil supplies
